## Why

Offline fixtures can establish the rubric's discrimination, but the epic succeeds only when the
deployed Gerrit review bot loads the criterion from the reviewed rebar repository and carries it
through the real four-pass pipeline. The first rollout must collect evidence without blocking
contributors.

A live Gerrit probe is required because only the deployed bot's webhook-to-checkout-to-prompt path
can prove end-to-end project-criterion execution; an offline replay would mock or bypass the
repository-resolution behavior this story is intended to dogfood.

## What

Run an advisory-only Gerrit dogfood probe after the seam repair and project criterion land. Use one
Gerrit change with four sequential patchsets against the review-system prompt surface:

1. A positive control adds this exact discovery/evidence refinement: `Before emitting, isolate
   the shortest changed clause that directs a review phase to act. Name the instructed phase, the
   assigned action, and the phase that owns that action. If the changed text does not identify all
   three, abstain instead of inferring an ownership violation.` The boundary criterion emits no
   finding.
2. Preserve the historical severity-only probe unchanged: `For each candidate finding, assign
   severity as high, medium, or low.` Record that it abstains because it does not identify the
   instructed and owning phases; this is evidence about stimulus limits, not criterion execution.
3. Use the predeclared balanced-corpus FIRE control RP-F2: `Pass 1 sets severity, confidence,
   blocking status, and remediation for every finding.` Capture the project-attributed advisory
   finding and its Pass-2/Pass-3 data.
4. A final patchset removes the FIRE sentence, retains only the valid positive-control refinement,
   and is the sole revision submitted to `main`.

## Preconditions

Before the probe, an operator confirms the configured `gerrit` remote targets rebar's Gerrit and
that the deployed review bot posts `LLM-Review` results for this repository. Record the remote URL,
change id, patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, and bot vote/message on this ticket. If the bot is absent or
misconfigured, do not substitute an offline run: create an operational bug linked
`discovered_from`, mark this story blocked, and resume only after the live prerequisite is restored.
Allow 60 minutes after each patchset upload for its `LLM-Review` message; after that window, follow
the same operational-bug and blocked-story path.

For this story, an acceptable review trace is the `code_review_result_v2` payload from the ambient
ticket-store artifact titled `code-review: <change-id> @ <revision>`, pasted into a ticket comment.
It must contain the reviewed `revision`, `coverage.llm_ran: true`, and the `blocking`, `advisory`,
`dropped`, and `indeterminate` lists. The predeclared RP-F2 FIRE probe provides direct project-criterion execution
proof: its finding must carry `reviewer_id: code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries` and
`criteria: [project.review-phase-boundaries]`. The positive control is deliberately a comparative
observation—same Gerrit change, unchanged routing/bot, LLM coverage present, and no project-criterion
entry in any verdict list—not a claim about unavailable per-criterion forwarding counters.

## Scope

- Keep `blocking_enabled: false` for the entire probe. `block_threshold: 0.90` is recorded but
  inert; no change in this story enables blocking.
- Record Gerrit change id, each patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, vote/message, project criterion finding,
  Pass-2 validity/impact attributes, Pass-3 priority/decision/threshold/posture, and final amended
  patchset outcome as ticket comments.
- Confirm the project-only physical prompt id ran against the RP-F2 FIRE-control patchset SHA using
  its stamped `reviewer_id`; compare the positive and cleaned revisions using the same artifact
  schema without claiming a nonexistent execution-count field.
- Leave the repository with only valid review instructions. Threshold calibration and a future
  `blocking_enabled: true` decision require a separate ticket backed by accumulated real-review
  data; this story neither selects a lower threshold nor promotes the criterion.

This story is observational: it does not change the rubric in response to probe results. A rubric
or seam defect discovered by the probe is captured as a new ticket linked `discovered_from` and is
fixed only through that separately reviewed work.

If the historical severity-only directive abstains, preserve that patchset and trace unchanged.
Use only the already-committed RP-F2 balanced-corpus FIRE case as the discriminating follow-up; do
not tune or improvise a new probe. If RP-F2 does not produce the project-attributed finding, record
the unexpected trace, create a rubric/seam bug linked `discovered_from`, and mark this story blocked.

After the final patchset, post a calibration handoff comment on this ticket with the exact labels
`Priority distribution:` and `Blocking promotion: deferred`; the latter must name a future,
separately reviewed, data-backed posture ticket as the only path to enabling blocking.

Out of scope: changing the rubric, collecting multi-day adoption metrics, changing the impact
model, or enabling blocking.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] The Gerrit remote and review-bot precondition is recorded with remote URL,
  change id, patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, and bot vote/message before either probe is evaluated.
- [ ] Before and after all probe patchsets, project routing remains `block_threshold: 0.90` and
  `blocking_enabled: false`; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'import json; r=json.load(open(".rebar/criteria_routing.json"))["code_review"]["project.review-phase-boundaries"]; assert r["block_threshold"] == 0.90 and r["blocking_enabled"] is False'`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A positive-control Gerrit patchset is recorded with change id, patchset
  SHA, UTC timestamp, and an acceptable artifact payload with `coverage.llm_ran: true`. Routing and
  bot deployment are unchanged across the four patchsets, and no entry in `blocking`, `advisory`,
  `dropped`, or `indeterminate` names `project.review-phase-boundaries` for this valid
  discovery/evidence refinement; entries from unrelated criteria do not affect the comparison.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The historical severity-only patchset is recorded unchanged with change id,
  patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, sentence, and acceptable artifact payload. Its repeated abstention
  and absence from every project-attributed verdict bucket are recorded as a stimulus limitation,
  not treated as proof.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The predeclared RP-F2 FIRE-control patchset is recorded with change id,
  patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, exact corpus sentence, and an acceptable artifact payload. Its
  grounded `advisory` finding carries `reviewer_id: code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries`
  and `criteria: [project.review-phase-boundaries]`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The ticket comment records the project-attributed advisory entry's
  observed Pass-2 `validity`, `impact`, and at least two named `verification.binary` answers from
  the persisted artifact. These are observations from the run, not predeclared invariant values.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The ticket comment records the entry's observed Pass-3 `priority` and
  the deterministic routing outcome `decision: advisory`, `block_threshold: 0.90`, and
  `blocking_enabled: false`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] All negative directives are absent from the final submitted patchset, the
  project criterion emits no phase-boundary finding on that revision, and the recorded final
  revision contains only phase-compliant instructions. This fourth patchset of the same Gerrit
  change is the only probe revision submitted to `main`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A ticket comment contains the exact labels `Priority distribution:` with
  the observed Pass-3 values and `Blocking promotion: deferred` with an explicit handoff to a future,
  separately reviewed, data-backed posture ticket.
- [ ] The final cleaned dogfood change is landed on `main`; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'import subprocess; commits=subprocess.check_output(["git", "log", "origin/main", "--format=%H", "--grep=rebar-ticket: 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d"], text=True).split(); assert commits, "dogfood commit is not on origin/main"'`.

## Dependencies

Depends on the landed repository-root seam repair `3ba4-c0d1-1813-44a5` and the
project-criterion authoring story `225a-323c-a9f6-436b`. The former umbrella
`2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02` and child bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` were superseded and closed.
